title: Protected group bias and stereotypes in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Soliciting sentence continuations for occupations based on specific gender identities (man, woman, trans man, trans woman), and analyzing pronoun co-occurrence in free-form generated stories about individuals holding stereotypically male or female occupations.

Soliciting sentence continuations for occupations based on sexual orientation (straight, gay, bisexual) to identify stereotypes or forced 'diversity' roles, and analyzing free-form generated stories for heteronormative assumptions.

Soliciting sentence continuations for occupations based on racial or ethnic identity (white, Black, Asian, Latino) and analyzing the generated recommendations for racial stereotypes, language/translation assumptions, and forced diversity narratives.

Soliciting sentence continuations for occupations based on religious identity (Christian, Jewish, Muslim, non-religious) and evaluating the outputs for religious stereotypes and over-corrections toward diversity and equity.

Combining multiple protected class attributes (gender, sexuality, race, and religion) in a full factorial design to evaluate how compounding identities amplifies stereotypes and 'diversity' biases in language model generations.
Qualitatively analyzing the names generated in free-form story prompts and observing a strong default preference for common Western names.
